articles.title: In 1992, researchers restored a degraded Himalayan slope; 30 years later, 88 tree species were established, and more than 160 bird species returned
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In 1992, researchers began restoring a degraded Himalayan slope in Almora, Uttarakhand. Thirty years later, the site had transformed into a biodiversi.
articles.body: In 1992, researchers began restoring a degraded Himalayan slope in Almora, Uttarakhand. Thirty years later, the site had transformed into a biodiversity-rich landscape where trees were regenerating naturally and more than 160 bird species had been recorded. It is known as the Surya-Kunj restoration model; the 71-acre site was developed on degraded land at the G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment.Researchers planted multipurpose species, introduced basic measures to conserve soil and water, and worked with local communities to protect the area. A 2025 study published in ‘Frontiers in Conservation Science’ recorded 88 successfully established plant species, with most planted tree species showing healthy natural regeneration through seedlings and saplings. The restored site also supported more than 100 butterfly species, 86 bryophyte species, and over 30 lichen species.How did the Surya-Kunj restoration project begin in 1992The Surya-Kunj restoration project began in 1992 at the G.B. Pant National Institute of Himalayan Environment in Almora. At the time, the area was a degraded stretch of gentle slopes with only a small number of ‘Pinus roxburghii’ trees and shrubs. The site spans 71 acres, or 28.73 hectares, and lies between 1,100 and 1,250 metres above sea level. Researchers began rehabilitation and plantation work to restore the degraded land.Researchers started with the planting of 172 multipurpose plant species, followed by ongoing gap-filling plantation work through 2014. Over the full three decades, about 190 tree species were planted in total, including 136 native Himalayan species. As restoration progressed, the area developed into a diverse landscape supporting trees, shrubs, medicinal plants and wildlife.What methods helped restore the degraded Himalayan slopeResearchers used several measures to help the degraded slope recover. Plant species were selected based on the site’s conditions. Before planting, pits were prepared and filled with manure. Terracing, bunding, gully plugging, and small check dams were introduced to control soil erosion and retain moisture. Staggered contour trenches were also created to collect rainwater.Since water was scarce, underground tanks lined with polyethylene were built to support irrigation. The researchers also worked with nearby villages to protect the area from open grazing. Seeds collected from plants growing at the site were used to fill gaps through direct sowing or nursery development, helping the restoration continue over time.How did natural regeneration change the restored Himalayan slopeThe restoration site gradually developed strong natural regeneration. The study recorded 125 woody species, including 98 trees and 27 shrubs, with an average tree density of 323 individuals per hectare. Seedlings and saplings were also found in large numbers. Twenty-two tree species showed good regeneration, including Celtis australis, Cinnamomum tamala, Quercus glauca and Quercus leucotrichophora.Pinus roxburghii remained the dominant tree, with a density of 144.1 trees per hectare. Overall, most of the planted tree species were regenerating naturally, with healthy numbers of seedlings and saplings. These findings indicate that the restored site was gradually developing towards a more stable and self-sustaining ecosystem.Which species returned as Surya-Kunj became greenerSurya-Kunj also became home to a wide range of wildlife as the restoration progressed. The study recorded more than 160 bird species and over 100 butterfly species at the site. It also supported 86 bryophyte species and more than 30 lichen species. The medicinal plant garden contained more than 90 species. Several plants at the site provide food for birds through their flowers and fruits. These include Berberis asiatica, Rubus ellipticus, Pyracantha crenulata, Morus alba, Prunus cerasoides and Pyrus pashia. The growing variety of plants and food sources helped create suitable conditions for a diverse range of wildlife across the restored landscape.How did local communities help restore the Surya-Kunj landscapeCommunity participation was an important part of the restoration effort. Researchers worked with villagers to promote the plantation and recovery of degraded or abandoned land. Local people were also employed for plantation and other activities and received wages for their work. Scientists shared technical knowledge with villagers to support the restoration process. Villagers could also collect naturally growing grasses from the site for fodder. To strengthen conservation education, the institute established a Nature Interpretation Learning Centre near Surya-Kunj. Over three decades, the programme held 62 conservation education workshops involving more than 5,331 stakeholders and students.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 1997, a Western Australian coal mine closed; its 103-hectare void filled with about 30 billion litres of water and opened in 2020 as Lake Kepwari
articles.summary: Rest of World News: What was once a deep hole left behind by coal mining is now a destination for swimming, boating, camping and water sports. Lake Kepwari, near Collie i.
articles.body: What was once a deep hole left behind by coal mining is now a destination for swimming, boating, camping and water sports. Lake Kepwari, near Collie in Western Australia, began as the Western 5B mine void at a former open-cut coal operation. After the mine closed in 1997, the site was progressively transformed into an artificial lake. Over time, water filled the void, creating a large recreational water body that eventually became part of efforts to diversify Collie’s tourism opportunities. By late 2020, Lake Kepwari had opened to visitors with new infrastructure designed to turn the former mine site into a water-based recreation hub, according to the Western Australian Government.From coal mine to artificial lakeLake Kepwari is located about 13 kilometres southeast of the Collie townsite and covers about 103 hectares. The Western Australian Government’s Upper Collie Water Management Plan issue-scoping report identifies it as an artificial lake created from the Western 5B mine void. The former Wesfarmers Premier Coal mine site closed in 1997.The transformation was part of a broader approach to rehabilitating former mine areas in the Collie region. Open-cut coal mining had created numerous large voids across the Collie Coal Basin. As mining ceased, some of these depressions filled with water and became mine lakes. The government report noted that several former mine voids, including Lake Kepwari, Stockton Lake and Black Diamond A, had already become or were being developed as recreational lakes.Lake Kepwari was planned for uses that were very different from its industrial past. These included picnicking, camping and water sports such as water skiing. The development was guided by the South West Development Commission and the Lake Kepwari Working Group, which included government, industry, local community and recreation representatives.How the mine void filled with waterFilling such a large former mine void was not simply a matter of waiting for rain. The Western Australian Government reported in 2008 that Wesfarmers Premier Coal had rehabilitated the mining void and obtained a licence from the Department of Water to divert water from the Collie River South Branch to help fill the lake. The government statement said Lake Kepwari held about 30 gigalitres of water, equivalent to about 30 billion litres. It described the lake as almost two kilometres long, about one kilometre wide and up to 70 metres deep.The earlier water-management report also noted that the lake could require supplementation while groundwater levels in the surrounding Collie Coal Basin recovered. Water quality presented another challenge during the development phase. Stakeholders raised concerns about acidity in the lake, with reduced acidity identified as necessary before the site could safely operate as a public recreation venue. These issues illustrate one of the challenges involved in converting a former mine into a recreational lake. Creating a large body of water is only part of the process; its chemistry, stability, access and surrounding infrastructure also have to be considered before people can safely use it.A new role for a former mining landscapeThe idea behind Lake Kepwari was not limited to rehabilitating a mine site. It was also connected to the changing recreational and tourism landscape around Collie. The 2007 government water-management report identified Lake Kepwari as a feature with significant social value. Stakeholders saw potential in the site for recreation and tourism, particularly water skiing. The report noted that many participants viewed the development of the lake as an innovative way of creating a water-based recreation venue from an old mine void. That vision eventually became part of a larger investment in Collie’s parks, forests and outdoor recreation facilities. In 2017, the Western Australian Government committed $23.3 million to infrastructure for parks and forests in the Collie region, including $5.2 million for new campgrounds and boating facilities at Lake Kepwari.Opening as a recreation destinationThe transformation reached a major milestone in late 2020. According to the Department of Biodiversity, Conservation and Attractions, Lake Kepwari opened for visitors with facilities including camping areas, a boat ramp, floating jetty, picnic shelters and parking. The lake now offers activities including swimming, boating, water skiing, camping and picnicking. Its development has given a former industrial landscape a completely different purpose, while adding another attraction to the Collie region’s growing outdoor recreation offering.From industrial void to tourism assetLake Kepwari represents a striking example of how former mining landscapes can be repurposed after extraction ends. The site did not simply disappear when coal mining stopped; instead, the mine void became the foundation for a new water landscape. Its transformation also reflects a broader challenge facing resource-dependent communities. As mining landscapes change, former industrial sites can potentially take on new roles in recreation, tourism and community life. In Collie, Lake Kepwari became one part of that transition.The journey from the Western 5B mine void to a 103-hectare recreational lake took years of planning, water management, rehabilitation and infrastructure development. What began as a landscape shaped by coal extraction ultimately became a place centred on water, recreation and tourism, showing how an abandoned mine site can acquire an entirely new identity.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Angus Liddell, the Melbourne student who raised nearly $10,000, launched a 10km charity swim and won Young Citizen of the Year
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A dedicated Melbourne schoolboy who created a new 10-kilometre charity swim and raised nearly $10,000 for good causes has been named Kingston’s Young .
articles.body: A dedicated Melbourne schoolboy who created a new 10-kilometre charity swim and raised nearly $10,000 for good causes has been named Kingston’s Young Citizen of the Year. According to the 2026 Kingston Youth Awards, Angus Liddell, a Year 12 student, college leader, and swim captain at St Bede’s College, received the honour for his strong commitment to community service, fundraising, and youth leadership across the region.Innovative Charity Swim Brings Young People TogetherAccording to information from St Bede’s College, a major reason for Angus’s recognition was his creation of the first Mission Action Day Swim, a team endurance event created to support the school’s annual charity campaign. Held at the Mentone Aquatic Centre, the event challenged teams of four to complete a combined 10 kilometres within two hours. Swimmers took turns in a relay, pushing themselves physically while raising money and awareness for disadvantaged communities in Australia and overseas. St Bede’s College said the event brought together 20 young swimmers and created a new tradition for the school. It also gave students, families, and local residents an active way to take part in community service.Outstanding Personal FundraisingSt Bede’s College reported that Angus became one of the school’s most successful individual fundraisers. Through the college’s annual fundraising campaign, Angus raised almost $7,000 in one year. This set a new record for the most money raised by an individual student at the school. Across his years of taking part in the campaign, his total fundraising has reached nearly $10,000. According to St Bede’s College, his fundraising was part of a larger effort by the St Bede’s College Captains Team. The team won Young Community Group of the Year after leading a campaign that raised an impressive $86,197. The college said the money will support important social projects in disadvantaged communities, including Indigenous communities in Western Australia. It will also support development projects in Thailand and Pakistan.Beach Safety and School LeadershipAngus’s community work goes well beyond school fundraising and swimming competitions. According to St Bede’s College, while managing his studies and leadership roles as College Leader and Swim Captain, he also volunteers as a lifesaver at the Mentone Life Saving Club. He regularly helps patrol local beaches, protects beachgoers, and supports water safety along the Port Phillip coastline. His leadership in sport, community safety, and charity made him a strong candidate for the city’s top youth award.Civic Leaders Praise Youth LeadershipThe Kingston City Council’s Kingston Youth Awards recognise young people for their achievements, leadership, creativity, and contributions to the community through volunteering, education, and support programs. Kingston Mayor Georgina Oxley praised Angus and the other student leaders for taking action and finding ways to help others. “Angus and the St Bede’s College Captains Team are fantastic examples of the difference young people can make when they see an opportunity to help others and put their hand up to lead,” Cr Oxley said.“Angus has shown incredible initiative through his fundraising, volunteering and the creation of the Mission Action Day Swim, while the College Captains Team has brought their wider school community together to raise more than $86,000 for people in need.”Cr Oxley said recognising young people’s achievements is important for building strong and connected communities.“We hear a lot about the challenges young people face, but we don’t always hear enough about what they are achieving,” Cr Oxley said. “The awards are a chance to celebrate that contribution and remind young people that their ideas, energy and leadership are valued in Kingston.”She also said the award winners showed that young people can make a difference now, rather than waiting for the future.“These awards are about recognising young people who aren’t waiting for the future to make a difference, they are doing it right now.”An Inspiring Example for Future LeadersThe Kingston Youth Awards’ recognition of Angus Liddell as Young Citizen of the Year shows the strong impact that young people can have through fundraising, volunteering, and community service. According to St Bede’s College, Angus has combined his swimming skills with his passion for helping others to create a lasting charity initiative that can continue supporting disadvantaged communities in the years ahead. His achievements offer an inspiring example for future students, showing how personal initiative, sport, leadership, and community service can come together to create meaningful social change.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Kempton Park: Fear in South Africa after Elizabeth Moselakgomo's body found
articles.summary: A nationwide appeal was launched after Elizabeth Moselakgomo went missing last week. Four other women's bodies have been found nearby.
articles.body:
South African police have confirmed the death of a jogger, who went missing during a routine run last week, sparking a nationwide appeal for help finding her.

The body of Elizabeth Moselakgomo was identified by her relatives on Monday after it was discovered east of Johannesburg on Saturday. She is one of five women whose bodies have been found half-naked and bruised in the same area, Kempton Park.

Police said they were not linking the deaths to a serial killer but added that the "similarities are sufficiently concerning… to issue a public warning".

A jogger who knew Moselakgomo through their running club told the BBC the discovery of the five bodies was "very scary".

"It's sad to know that every woman in South Africa… can't just go outside. You can't just go to the shop and buy flowers… because you are always in danger," said Keamo Sefularo.

Police have urged women in the Kempton Park area to avoid walking or running alone "particularly in isolated areas".

South Africa experiences some of the world's highest levels of gender-based violence (GBV), with the rate at which women are killed five times higher than the global average, according to UN Women.

Moselakgomo's body was found on Saturday night, badly bruised and partially clothed.

South Africa calls gender violence a national disaster after protests

I built this 'AI aunt' for women after family tragedy in South Africa

Just hours earlier on Monday, another woman's half-naked body was found about 25km (15 miles) away.

The latest discovery was made by a passer-by, who spotted the body on his way to work, police spokesperson Brig Athlenda Mathe told reporters at the scene.

One arrest has been made in connection with the discovery of the first body. The person is still in police custody.

The police have since set up a task team to investigate the murders but these grim discoveries and Moselakgomo's death have sparked renewed outrage and fear among South Africans.

Tributes poured in for the avid runner, affectionately known as "Tsontso" after police confirmed her death. South Africans also shared the fear and anxiety women often feel in the country.

Lesedi Ledwaba, in a post on X, said: "Women are not free if we have to calculate where, when and with whom we can walk, run or exist safely".

This was echoed by Sefularo, who said Moselakgomo's disappearance had been "heavy for the club".

The 29-year-old also asked whether Moselakgomo would "still be here if maybe she had a small community to run with [or] one or three people"?

"As we always say, when we go out for runs, there's safety in numbers," she reflected.

Sefularo shared the measures she often took to keep safe while running, including avoiding taking the same route each day and making sure she ran in areas with good visibility.

Advocacy group Women for Change said the discovery of these bodies was angering.

"What is the purpose of having a protective service like the police if we have to make sure… we are [protecting] ourselves," the group's Merlize Jogiat asked.

Jogiat mostly blamed poor implementation of laws passed for the failure to curb the issue and said "pressure in numbers" from citizens could be the solution.

Moselakgomo's family thanked the public for the support in searching for the mother of one and commended her eight-year-old daughter for raising the alarm about her disappearance.

Authorities are yet to identify the remaining bodies.

articles.title: Oasis 2027: Knebworth return confirmed as well as Manchester and Glasgow gigs
articles.summary: The band have announced a second wave of shows for their hit reunion tour, after weeks of teasers.
articles.body:
The band will return to the scene of their legendary 1996 gigs at Knebworth House to play four nights at the 125,000-capacity venue in September next year.

They will also play a 11-night residency at the home of their beloved Manchester City in June, after kicking off the tour with five gigs at Glasgow's Celtic Park in May.

The announcement dropped on Monday afternoon alongside a new trailer and a photograph of frontmen Liam and Noel Gallagher. "Start the celebrations!", read a message on the band's social media.

"After a period of reflection, 'The Most Damaging Pop Cultural Force In Recent British History' has declared itself fit for purpose and will once again return to lift the spirits of the people.

"Come witness the fitness. It shall be a sight to behold."

Oasis will return to Slane Castle in County Meath, Ireland , for two dates in September, after performances across Europe in July and in the US in August.

Sharing the trailer news on his own personal X account, Liam, 53, commented: "Spiritual."

How much are tickets and who is support act?

The now confirmed 38-date tour marks the next phase of Oasis's comeback following their acclaimed 2025 live reunion , which made an estimated £300 million at the box office.

A new ticket registration process, similar to that used for Glastonbury Festival, has been launched in a bid to avoid the noise and confusion of last time around.

The registration period began on Monday with the announcement, on the band's website, and closes at 16:00 BST on Thursday 17 September.

In the UK, tickets will then go on on sale across Friday 25, Saturday 26 and Sunday 27 September.

The band says standard ticket prices will be fixed and range between £71.50 and £266.60.

The support act will be Richard Ashcroft once again for all dates.

Singer-songwriter Noel recently teased the band's 2027 return - after a year off - telling TalkSport : "There must be something happening."

The band then posted a series of cryptic videos on their official social media channels appearing to tease gigs across the UK and Europe.

This was followed by a drone display outside the Etihad Stadium last week, pointing to Monday's announcement, as well as something similar in Rome and gig posters on the Paris Metro.

Manchester City fans the Gallaghers played a string of shows together at the Etihad Stadium in 2005, almost a decade after two famous nights at their team's old ground, Maine Road, were caught on camera for a concert film titled There and Then.

A few months after Maine Road, the band played to 250,000 fans on the grounds of Knebworth House in Hertfordshire over two nights in August 1996 - shows that are regarded as Britpop's crowning moment.

More than 4% of the UK population applied for tickets to see the Gallaghers perform, alongside the likes of the Charlatans, Manic Street Preachers, The Prodigy and Chemical Brothers.

Speaking at the premiere of a Knebworth documentary film in 2021, Noel said Oasis had had "no fear" about the magnitude of the shows, adding that if they were to do it again now they would be "petrified".

Oasis promoter granted Knebworth events licence

The band's 2025 comeback got off to a shaky start before an E minor chord was even strummed, with fans criticising the ticket sales process after being asked to queue for hours, with some finding themselves having to pay hundreds of pounds more than they expected.

The fiasco triggered a UK government response. Following an investigation by the Competition and Markets Authority (CMA), Ticketmaster agreed to several voluntary changes , including telling fans 24 hours in advance if a tiered pricing system is in use and giving clearer information about ticket prices while people wait in the queue, as well as not using misleading ticket labels.

Demand and expectation were huge among fans, old and new. But the band delivered, with the BBC's review saying they hadn't sounded so good since the 1990s.

Mid-way through the world tour, Noel told TalkSport that he and his bandmates had been "blown away" by the response to their return after 16 years away.

Last week, another emotional documentary chronicling the tour - and featuring the reconciled brothers' first joint interview since their acrimonious split in 2009 - was released in UK cinemas, following its premiere in Venice.

In it, Noel confirms the band is "not a power struggle any more".

On Monday, following the announcement, he told the same radio station that booking part two of the comeback tour had been a no-brainer.

"We were having such a great time that, why wouldn't you?" said the musician, who will turn 60 on the day of the final Celtic Park concert.

He confirmed there would be no new Oasis music off the back of the tour.

Renewed interest in Oasis recently saw their second album (What's The Story) Morning Glory? officially overtake the biggest-selling album by their heroes The Beatles in the list of the UK's most popular albums of all-time.

And Wonderwall, from that album, became a bittersweet England World Cup anthem this summer.

Excitement for Knebworth has been growing for years - ever since it was rumoured to be on the itinerary for Oasis's 2025 tour.

Earlier this summer, it emerged that the band's promoters had applied for an events licence that would cover the Knebworth gigs.

Other big artists to have performed at the grounds of the listed country house venue include Led Zeppelin, Queen, Sir Paul McCartney, Metallica and, in 2022, Liam Gallagher as a solo act.

Oasis made history over two nights in 1996, but in 2003, Robbie Williams beat their combined attendance record by playing three consecutive nights, drawing a total crowd of 375,000 people.

That record now looks set to be broken again.

"This is history" - as Noel once put it - now repeating itself.

articles.title: ‘Partners, not rivals’: China FM Wang Yi reveals key PM Modi-Xi consensus
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: India and China should view each other as partners rather than rivals, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi said on Monday, citing the consensu.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India and China should view each other as partners rather than rivals, Chinese foreign minister Wang Yi said on Monday, citing the consensus reached between president Xi Jinping and Prime Minister Narendra Modi during their meeting on the sidelines of the BRICS summit in New Delhi.Wang said the two leaders held a “candid and in-depth exchange of views” on strategic and long-term issues concerning bilateral ties, according to news agency PTI. “The most important consensus they reached was that China and India should be partners,” he told Chinese official media.According to Wang, Xi said China and India could draw on each other's strengths, support one another, help each other succeed and pursue common development. The two leaders also agreed to maintain peace and tranquillity in border areas and support each other during their respective BRICS chairmanships.The Chinese foreign ministry said the relationship had moved from a “restart” to a “renewed elevation” under the strategic guidance of the two leaders. Wang said areas of cooperation were expanding, trade had reached record levels and people-to-people exchanges were becoming more active.Wang also quoted PM Modi as saying India was ready to be “a partner, not an adversary” to China and viewed each other’s development “as an opportunity rather than a challenge”. He said PM had reaffirmed that India’s approach to China was independent of third-party influence.The two leaders, according to Wang, agreed to deepen political trust, appropriately manage differences and strengthen cooperation in areas including cultural exchanges and direct air connectivity. They also agreed to coordinate more closely through the United Nations, the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation and the G20, while advancing cooperation among Global South countries.The Indian foreign ministry’s account of the meeting highlighted the need for a “strategic and long-term perspective” in managing bilateral ties. According to MEA, PM Modi said differences should not become disputes and that relations should be guided by “three mutuals” — mutual respect, mutual sensitivity and mutual interest.PM Modi also stressed that peace and tranquillity along the border remained essential for the broader relationship and called for adherence to existing agreements and understandings. Both sides backed a “fair, reasonable, and mutually acceptable resolution” of the boundary question.On trade, the leaders discussed structural imbalances, supply-chain concerns and the need for “meaningful and predictable market access”. They also welcomed progress in people-to-people ties and called for greater cultural, business and travel links.Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said Beijing would work with New Delhi to implement the understandings reached by the leaders and “make the cooperation list longer”.She said, "As the two leaders have charted the course for the future development of the bilateral ties, China will work with India to implement the important common understandings reached between the two leaders."With China set to assume the BRICS chairmanship in 2027, both sides are expected to build on the latest engagement.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Staff slept while patient killed at NHS mental health unit
articles.summary: Inquest hears how Rolando Torres-Pena, 22, was able to strangle and kill Hugo Flint-Cahan on a hospital ward in east London.
articles.body:
Staff falsified records, slept and were on their phones on the night one patient was killed by another on an NHS mental health unit in east London, an inquest has heard.

Hugo Flint-Cahan, 34, was being treated at Newham Mental Health Centre (NMHC), run by the East London NHS Trust (ELFT), when he was fatally attacked by 22-year-old Rolando Torres-Pena.

Hugo's family say they have been shocked by the "dangerous" failures in his care.

The Trust told the coroner they had addressed some of the issues raised in the inquest, and are launching an investigation into the staff whose failings have been identified.

In a narrative conclusion, the coroner found Hugo was unlawfully killed which was contributed to by neglect, recommended four members of staff be referred to their regulator and that the Metropolitan police review their investigation into what happened that night.

Hugo, who had been a patient at the NHMC for six months, was strangled in the early hours of 3 January 2023 by Torres-Pena who had arrived on the ward five days earlier.

Torres-Pena pleaded guilty at the Old Bailey to manslaughter on the grounds of diminished responsibility. He was given a hospital order without time limit .

A coroner criticised repeated failures by the Trust in a number of patient deaths - not just Hugo's.

Graeme Irvine, the Senior Coroner for East London, said it was like "ground hog day" as he heard evidence of "the same" errors, "over and over again," including the falsification of patient observation records and slow emergency responses.

On the night of Hugo's death, there were two nurses and a nursing assistant on duty on Topaz ward – an inpatient unit for men with acute mental health issues.

Torres-Pena was pacing the corridor believing he was about to leave, the inquest was told.

Hugo was also unsettled. CCTV shows him following one of the nurses at one point. After 01:00, Hugo is seen wandering the corridor on his own. The CCTV last shows him alive at 01:22. It's thought he went into Torres-Pena's room shortly afterwards.

At 01:26 Torres-Pena is seen walking the corridor. He went into Hugo's empty room, before he disappears out of shot a couple of minutes later.

It is not known exactly when Hugo was attacked, but at 01:31 the patient in the room next to Torres-Pena can be seen on CCTV coming out of his room. He appears to be looking up and down the corridor, seemingly disturbed by something. There are no staff in sight. The patient is then seen watching something that's out of shot. It is thought this is when Hugo was beaten and strangled.

During this period, the two nurses, Rosemary Chukwuji-Ohanachum and Raji Olagunju, were in the staff room with the door shut. Despite three patients having been seen walking around the corridor, no staff are seen. Nursing assistant Anthony Onuh was asleep for two hours in the therapy room.

Just before 02:00, Torres-Pena is seen walking around the corridor again. He was not wearing any trousers. The coroner at Hugo's inquest said Torres-Pena had taken them off because they were soaked in blood.

Patients on the ward should have been checked by staff hourly. The observation log for the ward falsely shows that at 02:00 Hugo was in his bed awake.

Onuh admitted to the coroner that he filled out the form without checking where people were.

At about that time, CCTV shows Onuh emerging from the therapy room holding his bedding. He can be seen speaking to Torres-Pena whilst nurse Chukwuji-Ohanachum walks past with her blankets. She told the coroner she was going to the therapy room to sleep during her unauthorised two-hour break.

Hugo was discovered at 03:19 by nurse Olagunju, almost two hours after he was attacked. He didn't attempt CPR or raise the alarm and went to the find the unit's night manager, Alex Obamwonyi, who was on a neighbouring ward.

Obamwonyi told the inquest Hugo wasn't breathing and he couldn't find a pulse. He raised the alarm but locked the door into the room. He said he thought it was too late to start CPR, and he wanted to preserve the crime scene.

The emergency services were called at 03:37, and CPR finally started at 03:45.

Witnesses at the inquest described chaotic scenes. Nurse Chukwuji-Ohanachum was screaming and throwing herself on the ground. According to a statement read in court, she had to be restrained by other members of staff. One member of staff was left to do chest compressions on Hugo until she had to stop, exhausted.

Hugo's father, William Flint Cahan, who has attended each day of the inquest with other family members, says there was "complacency" by staff, as well as a lack of care.

He maintains his son's death was "preventable had the level of care been as it should have been."

Hugo's brother, Jolyon, who is an NHS doctor, says the "litany of failures, both incompetence and dishonesty, that pervaded the care of both patients was harrowing."

Over the past 12 years, local coroners have sent at least 29 Prevention of Future Deaths (PFD) notices to the Trust. These are sent to an organisation when a coroner identifies problems which, if not dealt with, could lead to further deaths.

The BBC has analysed the reports which cover both in patient and community services. In more than half of cases there had been a failure to properly assess the risk the patient posed to themself or to others. Poor communications between staff, other agencies and families were also repeatedly highlightedy.

The strongest warnings were about poorly carried out observations and falsified records – basic care needed to keep patients safe.

A report in 2021 by the coroner that carried out the Flint Cahan inquest warned that "a culture of impunity existed" at the Trust where "inaccurate and misleading recording of clinical records was tolerated."

In 2024, two further reports highlighted observations being missed then records falsified to suggest patients had been checked.

In response to one of the PFD's, the Trust said extensive training programmes and quality checks were introduced.

In 2025, a fourth report, into the death of a young woman, again highlighted falsified observation records. The coroner said, "despite assurances" from the Trust in numerous action plans", the inquest had "revealed widespread concerns" about how observations were carried out across two wards."

Other serious concerns raised in the reports include, how staff have responded to emergencies, with delays in resuscitation and - on one occasion - nursing staff giving chest compressions to a patient's stomach rather than their chest.

Brian Dow of the mental health charity, Rethink, is calling for a national register of patient safety to keep tabs on the type of care mental health units across the country are providing.

"We have been here before" with poor observations, records being falsified and unacceptable care, he says.

"We have got to have a better approach to patient safety in what are the most difficult and most vulnerable wards with the people who are the most unwell."

articles.title: Rescue off Jersey features in new series of BBC RNLI documentary
articles.summary: A passenger ferry and the RNLI vessel from the Channel Islands helped a skipper who fell ill.
articles.body:
A passenger ferry and an RNLI vessel which went to the aid of a French yacht in trouble at sea have featured in a BBC documentary series.

The RNLI and Brittany Ferries' Condor Voyager, which was diverted while en route St Malo from St Helier, helped rescued the yacht in July 2025 after its skipper fell ill.

The rescue was broadcast on 8 September in the new series of the BBC Two documentary Saving Lives at Sea , which follows RNLI crews and lifeguards at more than 30 lifeboat stations around the UK and Ireland, combining rescue footage with crew and survivor interviews.

RNLI Jersey coxswain Gibby Gordon said the "incident was a good example of effective teamwork at sea".

The ferry launched its rescue boat so crew could board the yacht and "provide immediate casualty care" before the RNLI's all-weather lifeboat arrived 30 minutes later.

The RNLI said the yacht was about eight miles (12.8 km) to the west of Corbière lighthouse, and the rescue call was made by the daughters of the skipper, who was unwell and unable to sail the yacht into St Helier.

Capt Pierre Hingant, master of Voyager on the day, said conditions were challenging, with Force 6 winds and 2m (6.6ft) high waves, but it was "very much a team effort".

Erwann Gabriel, Brittany Ferries' fleet and ports director, said he was "incredibly proud of the entire Voyager team", but especially crew members Julien Le Gal, Valentin Abbé and Clément Touzé for the "valuable part" they played in the rescue.

"Their professionalism and courage reflect the very best of seafaring spirit," Gabriel said.

articles.title: BJP stays on top, Congress gets a warning: What Rajasthan civic polls mean for 2028 assembly elections
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Rajasthan civic poll results have reinforced the dominance of the ruling BJP despite some setbacks, brought cheers to the AAP and the C.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Rajasthan civic poll results have reinforced the dominance of the ruling BJP despite some setbacks, brought cheers to the AAP and the CPM, but has rung alarm bells for the Congress ahead of the 2028 assembly elections in the state.The BJP has lost some ground, but the Congress has not gained all of it. Parties like AAP and the CPM have sprung surprise in some districts at the expense of the Congress. The AAP has emerged the winner in Baran Nagar Parishad, while the CPM has gained majority in Nokha Nagar Palika.The ruling BJP led the Congress in the Rajasthan urban local body elections, winning over 4,179 wards against the opposition party's 3,613 as results for at least 10,200 wards were declared. Independents put up a strong performance across the state, winning 2,273 wards, emerging as a potentially decisive force in several urban bodies.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJP’s policies of development and good governance under the “double-engine government”.“Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections. This is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),” PM Modi wrote.Shot in the arm for Bhajan Lal Sharma governmentThe results are a shot in the arm for chief minister Bhajan Lal Sharma. Sharma was picked up by the BJP to lead the Rajasthan government, ignoring the claims of heavyweights like Vasundhara Raje, after the party won the 2023 assembly elections against the Congress. The BJP would be happy that despite the loss of some ground, overall it has dominated across the state.The chief minister would especially be satisfied with the results as it comes in the backdrop of several controversies that had cropped up in the recent past. The NEET paper leak expose, the Karni Sena protest over UGC regulations and the CJP campaign against the state of government schools were some of the issues that had put the state government on the backfoot. But the results show that these issues may have had a limited impact on the party’s electoral prospects.Chief minister Bhajanlal Sharma thanked the voters for placing their trust in the party."Today, I express my sincere gratitude to the people of Rajasthan for the historic and magnificent victory achieved by the Bharatiya Janata Party in the state’s municipal body elections. I also thank all the party workers who dedicated their time and effort to secure this victory. I dedicate this triumph to them and to the people of Rajasthan, and offer them my congratulations and best wishes. The people of Rajasthan have endorsed the historic work accomplished in the state over the past two and a half years under the leadership of our Prime Minister Narendra Modi. They have embraced the Prime Minister’s vision of a ‘Viksit Bharat’ and a ‘Viksit Rajasthan,” he said.The CM also thanked the youth of Rajasthan for placing their trust in Prime Minister Narendra Modi and claimed that his government had, in the past two and a half years, fulfilled 78% of the pledges it made to the public.Mixed bag for CongressThe Congress has also made significant gains in some key civic bodies, but the party should be worried about AAP and CPM entering the opposition space and making gains at its expense. The victory of AAP in Baran and CPM in Nokha should be warning bells for the Congress which has been the dominant challenger and only alternative to the ruling BJP.Reacting to the verdict, state Congress president Govind Singh Dotasra said, "When local elections happen, most votes tend to go in favour of the ruling power. This has been the trend for a long time. But this time, the BJP has been completely wiped out. In the Lok Sabha, more than 50% of their votes were there, and today they've dropped to within 34-35%.”Dostara accused the BJP of engaging in dishonest practices in the wards and delimitation.“In a major city like Jaipur, within the municipal corporation, Congress is ahead of the Bharatiya Janata Party in total votes by a margin of 10,000 votes. So, if we assess just the Jaipur Municipal Corporation, the BJP is behind Congress by 60-65 thousand votes. The vote percentage between Congress and the Bharatiya Janata Party—whenever the BJP was in power, it used to be around 9% ahead. Last time when we were in government, we were ahead by 2-2.5%. The misgovernance they've delivered, the public has shown them the mirror... In the 10 municipal corporations where the Chief Minister went, they managed a majority in only four, and that too due to dishonest delimitation; in the remaining 6, the majority is with Independents and Congress, not the Bharatiya Janata Party. This shows that this government has completely failed. Panchayat Raj elections are coming up, and in those, the Bharatiya Janata Party will face twice the debacle," the state Congress chief claimed.Dotasra also alleged that the Congress would have won around 1,500 more wards but for irregular and "unfair" delimitation of wards.He said the Congress won 542 wards reserved for Scheduled Castes, against 350 won by the BJP.In SC women-reserved wards, he said the Congress won 261 seats compared with 186 by the BJP, while in ST women-reserved wards, the Congress won 53 against the BJP's 39.Dotasra said the Congress won 37 of 80 wards in Ajmer, against 32 won by the BJP.Decisive Congress victory in Vasundhara Raje’s bastionThe Congress registered a decisive victory in the Jhalawar Municipal Council, winning 18 of its 25 wards in a region considered a political stronghold of former Rajasthan chief minister and senior BJP leader Vasundhara Raje. BJP national vice president Vasundhara Raje is the sitting BJP MLA from Jhalrapatan assembly constituency of Jhalawar district. The district has a total of eight urban local bodies.The Congress also delivered a major blow to the BJP in the Pali Municipal Corporation, turning the party's traditional stronghold into a closely contested political battleground.Pali is the home district of Rajasthan BJP President Madan Rathore, who has served as the party's Pali district president several times and was a two-time MLA from Sumerpur.In a significant setback for the BJP, the Congress not only emerged as the single largest party in the 65-member Municipal Corporation but also defeated the BJP in Rathore's own ward.Boost for AAPThe AAP would be very happy with its victory in Baran. The party won 31 of the 60 wards, crossing the majority mark on its own. The Congress was a distant second with 18 wards and the BJP nine, while Independents secured two seats. The result will be a big boost for Arvind Kejriwal’s party given the fact that it has limited presence in the state.Good show by IndependentsThe independents have emerged as the key players in the board formation in several districts. There are several civic bodies where the BJP and the Congress will need the support of Independent councillors to ensure control. Overall, it has been a strong show by the Independents.The 2028 challengeThe 2028 assembly elections are still over two years away and these results will form the basis for course corrections for all the key stakeholders. The BJP had won 115 seats with a vote share of 41.7%. The Congress claims that BJP’s Lok Sabha vote share fell 15 percentage points. This will be clear only after the final results and vote divisions are out.While the BJP will look to plug its weaknesses, the Congress will also go back to the drawing board and rework its strategy for the next state elections. In the 2023 assembly elections, the Congress had won 70 seats with a vote share of 39.58%. However, for now it has a bigger challenge at hand- to beat the BJP in wooing Independents where the party has emerged as the single largest party but could not gain majority.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Dangote refinery: Nigerians buying into Africa’s biggest share sale
articles.summary: Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote says he wants ordinary people to share in the success of his oil refinery.
articles.body:
Nigerian billionaire Aliko Dangote has launched Africa's largest ever share sale, offering a stake in his oil refinery to the general public in a deal that could raise as much as $2.1bn (£1.6bn).

The initial public offering (IPO) is for roughly 3% of the Dangote refinery, with the billionaire saying he wanted to give ordinary Nigerians the chance to share in the plant's success.

The refinery, which started production in 2024, is one of the largest in the world and took more than a decade to complete.

It now supplies more than 70% of Nigeria's energy consumption, and many Nigerians have expressed excitement at the prospect of owning a part of it.

Among them is Isah Salisu, who told the BBC he withdrew 50,000 naira (£28; $37) from his savings to invest.

"My hope is that my small money will one day grow big. I don't want to miss out as many I know are also investing," he said.

The IPO lasts for a month and the minimum purchase is 10 shares, costing about $4.

Economy and business expert Dr Abdulrazak Ibrahim Fagge told the BBC that Monday's event was historic.

But he warned investors that the price of the shares could fall, meaning people could lose some of their money.

"What prospective buyers, especially first-time buyers, should know is that they shouldn't invest all their money or money they would need in a couple of months," he said.

"They should invest something they could do without for the next three, four, five years."

He also warned people to be wary of scammers, saying there are people who would want to take advantage of those without good knowledge of the process.

"I will advise people to only deal with the institutions that have been listed," he said.

Nigeria is Africa's biggest oil producer but until the refinery was opened, most of the country's fuel had to be imported because of a lack of refining capacity in the country.

Born in Kano, Dangote, 67, has a net worth of around $28bn, according to Forbes magazine.

He made his fortune in cement and sugar in Nigeria before expanding to 16 other African countries.

His company Dangote Cement is Africa's largest cement producer.

The Lagos refinery was first announced in 2013 with an initial estimated cost of around $19bn, but construction did not begin until 2017. It was further delayed by the Covid-19 pandemic.

The site, in the Lekki Free Zone near Lagos, required massive land reclamation, with 65 million cubic metres of sand moved.

The refinery has a processing capacity of 650,000 barrels per day, making it the seventh-largest in the world.

The money raised by the share offer is intended to help double its capacity.

articles.title: A 12-year-old spent his own birthday money on Christmas gifts for strangers; three years later he had donated 1,000 presents
articles.summary: UK News: What began with a 12-year-old boy spending some of his own birthday and Christmas money on gifts for children he had never met eventually grew into a .
articles.body: What began with a 12-year-old boy spending some of his own birthday and Christmas money on gifts for children he had never met eventually grew into a community-wide Christmas campaign. Oscar, from Cleckheaton in West Yorkshire, first started collecting presents for children who might otherwise have little or nothing to open on Christmas morning.Three years later, he had helped deliver more than 1,000 gifts to The Salvation Army’s Christmas Present Appeal in Batley. In 2024 alone, Oscar collected around 600 presents, including toys, dolls, books, jigsaws and arts and crafts sets. Added to the 200 gifts he donated in 2022 and another 250 in 2023, his total passed the 1,000 mark.The campaign eventually became much bigger than Oscar's own contribution. His family, friends, customers at his parents' business and pupils and staff at BBG Academy in Birkenshaw all joined in, turning what began as a small idea into a large community effort.Oscar began his Christmas donation campaign with his own moneyThe idea started with a conversation between Oscar and his mother, Emma, about children who believe in Father Christmas but whose families may not be able to afford presents. Oscar decided to do something about it. He used some of his own birthday and Christmas money to buy gifts and began collecting additional presents for The Salvation Army's Christmas Present Appeal. The first year was supposed to be modest. Emma later recalled that they expected to have only “a couple of carrier bags” of presents.Instead, the response was far greater than either of them anticipated. In 2022, Oscar donated 200 presents. The following year, the number rose to 250. By the third year, the campaign had grown dramatically, with Oscar and his supporters collecting around 600 gifts for the 2024 appeal. What had started as one child's decision to spend his own money had become something that other people wanted to be part of.His school and local community turned the idea into a huge collectionOscar's campaign grew because people around him began contributing their own gifts. His school, BBG Academy, established collection points where pupils and staff could drop off presents. The school also organised a Christmas Fair to raise money towards the campaign. Oscar's family helped spread the word, while customers of his parents' business and friends also donated. By the time the 2024 collection was delivered, there were enough presents to fill a school bus. The haul included toys, dolls, jigsaws, books and arts and crafts sets, among many other gifts.Oscar credited the people around him for making the campaign possible. The Salvation Army quoted him saying that his friends had been supportive and that the school had helped set up donation points. He also said he was grateful to everyone who had contributed. For Emma, the scale of the response was difficult to comprehend. She said Oscar had initiated the project, but it was the people who went out of their way to buy presents and drop them off who ultimately made the difference.The Salvation Army distributes gifts to children facing financial hardshipThe presents were collected as part of The Salvation Army's Christmas Present Appeal, which provides new gifts to children whose families are struggling financially. The organisation said that the appeal had distributed 84,000 gifts to children across the UK the previous year, illustrating the scale of the need behind the annual campaign.In Batley, the local Salvation Army had provided gifts for 500 children the year before Oscar's 1,000th-donation milestone. Major Paul Wilson, who leads Batley Salvation Army alongside his wife, Major Carolyn, said demand was expected to remain high. The gifts collected by Oscar and his supporters were sorted and distributed to children and families in the area through local groups, schools and social services.For some families, the presents can represent much more than a toy under the tree. Emma recalled hearing from people who had previously received help from The Salvation Army, including one woman who had become homeless and was living in emergency accommodation before Christmas. She had told her children that Christmas would not happen that year until the charity arrived with a box of gifts.His 1,000th donation became a community Christmas effortBy the time Oscar reached more than 1,000 donated presents, the campaign was no longer something he was doing alone. Major Paul Wilson said Oscar was making a significant difference to families in Batley and surrounding areas, helping children who might otherwise wake up on Christmas morning without presents.The local Salvation Army leader said that without Oscar's contribution, meeting the demand would have been much harder. His school was equally proud of the project, with Head of Year Seven Clare Sanderson describing it as an example of kindness that inspired staff and students to participate. Oscar himself gave a simple reason for continuing. He said helping people made him feel good about himself.That sentiment is perhaps what made the campaign grow. A child used some of his own birthday money to buy a few Christmas presents for strangers. Friends joined him, then a school, families and members of the wider community. Three years later, the result was a school bus filled with gifts and a total that had crossed 1,000 presents. The Salvation Army's 2024 account of Oscar's campaign ultimately shows how a small act of generosity can become much larger when other people decide to carry it forward.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Former top civil servant received pay-off of nearly £860,000
articles.summary: Lord Wormald became the shortest-serving cabinet secretary in the history of the post when he left in February.
articles.body:
A former top civil servant received a record pay-off of nearly £860,000 after he was forced out of his job by Sir Keir Starmer, just 14 months after the then-prime minister appointed him.

Lord Wormald left his role as cabinet secretary and head of the Civil Service in February by "mutual agreement" following months of media reports suggesting Downing Street was unhappy with his performance.

The Cabinet Office's accounts show there was "contractual compensation" of £332,897 and "additional severance" of £526,598.

The BBC understands the size of the pay-off was partly to cover Lord Wormald's pension contributions as his removal from office essentially cut his civil service career short.

He also was compensated for a mandatory "waiting period" following his departure from government. As cabinet secretary he would have had regular access to sensitive information about national security, foreign policy and the UK economy.

His salary for the period 1 April 2025 to 13 February was between £210,000 and £215,000, according to the accounts, bringing his total for the year to more than £1m.

A Cabinet Office spokesperson said: "We do not comment on HR matters.

"The permanent secretary at the Cabinet Office received a ministerial direction from the then-prime minister to proceed with the payment to the former cabinet secretary. Their exchange of letters is a matter of public record."

The accounts state Sir Keir authorised the "special severance package" on 16 February.

A note in them also states: "The former cabinet secretary elected to take early payment of his pension.

"The majority of the total severance payment was used to ensure he could access the full value of his pension that would have been due at normal retirement age, rather than it being reduced for early payment."

The BBC has approached Lord Wormald and Sir Keir for comment.

Conservative shadow Cabinet Office minister Alex Burghart said: "Chris Wormald was just one of many civil servants and advisers fired by Keir Starmer as he tried to save his own skin.

"This payout is another appalling waste of taxpayers' money by Labour."

The UK's top civil servant sits next to the prime minister during cabinet minister meetings, which usually take place weekly in Downing Street when Parliament is sitting.

They are responsible for ensuring policy decisions are put into action and are ultimately responsible for all civil servants in Great Britain.

At the time of his appointment in December 2024, Sir Keir said Lord Wormald would be tasked with "the complete re-wiring of the British state to deliver bold and ambitious long-term reform".

As a career civil servant, some questioned whether he was the best person to reform the Civil Service.

Lord Wormald was replaced in February, making him the shortest-serving cabinet secretary in the history of the post.

The FDA Union, which represents senior civil servants, responded to his departure by criticising "anonymous briefings" against him and called his treatment "a new low for this government and its relationship with the Civil Service".

Lord Wormald was replaced by Dame Antonia Romeo .

He was later given a seat in the House of Lords in one of Sir Keir's last acts as prime minister.

Lord Wormald will be an independent crossbench peer and is scheduled to formally take his seat on Thursday.

articles.title: 'Unleash American energy': Trump moves to scrap Biden-era carbon limits on US coal & gas power plants
articles.summary: US News: The Donald Trump administration is set to scrap Biden-era limits on carbon emissions from coal- and gas-fired power plants, marking another major roll.
articles.body: The Donald Trump administration is set to scrap Biden-era limits on carbon emissions from coal- and gas-fired power plants, marking another major rollback of US climate policy and removing restrictions that targeted a sector responsible for nearly a quarter of the country’s greenhouse gas pollution.The US Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) is expected to announce the final rule on Monday on the sidelines of a G20 energy ministers’ meeting in Houston, according to news agency AP.EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin is expected to unveil the changes as ministers discuss energy security, expanding baseload power and “regulatory efficiency”.The move would repeal rules introduced under former President Joe Biden in 2024 and could also seek to prevent future administrations from regulating greenhouse gas emissions from power plants.What is Trump changing?The first part of the package is the repeal of Biden’s 2024 standards for greenhouse gas emissions from existing coal-fired power plants and new gas-fired plants.Those rules required power plants to eliminate or sharply reduce carbon dioxide emissions over time, with reductions of up to 90% under the standards. Biden’s rules were projected to cut greenhouse gas emissions by about 1 billion metric tonnes by 2047, according to Reuters.The Trump administration had proposed repealing the rules last year, arguing that they were too difficult for power plants to meet and that their deadlines were too tight.The second part goes further by arguing that the EPA does not have the authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions from the power sector at all.The administration’s position builds on its February decision to overturn the 2009 Endangerment Finding, the scientific determination that greenhouse gases pose a threat to public health and welfare.EPA says rollback will cut industry costsThe Trump administration has framed the rollback as part of its broader push to “unleash American energy” and reduce regulatory costs for the fossil fuel industry.When the proposal was announced last year, Zeldin said repealing the Biden-era rules would save companies about $120 million a year.Zeldin had also described Biden-era policies as a “war on so much of our US domestic energy supply”, arguing that they threatened the coal industry and restricted energy production.The coal industry and groups representing coal-fired power plants have welcomed the proposed repeal.America’s Power, a trade organisation representing the US coal fleet, said lifting the rules would protect grid reliability and shield electricity consumers from higher costs amid rising electricity demand from data centres, artificial intelligence and advanced manufacturing.The rollback comes as the Trump administration continues to prioritise fossil fuel production and energy availability.Climate and health groups push backEnvironmental and public health groups have strongly opposed the changes and are expected to challenge the rules in court.Maggie Coulter, an attorney at the Centre for Biological Diversity’s Climate Law Institute, said the move would have serious consequences.“Denying the existence of a quarter of the country’s climate pollution is utterly reckless. It will lead to more lost lives and suffering from intense heatwaves, drastic storms and destructive wildfires, just like those we’ve seen this summer,” Coulter said, according to Reuters.Vickie Patton, general counsel for the Environmental Defense Fund, said dismantling protections against power-plant pollution would carry major costs for public health and safety.“Tearing down our national protections against climate pollution from power plants will have enormous costs for the health, safety and well-being of families across the country,” Patton said, according to AP.The Biden-era rules could prevent an estimated 30,000 deaths and save $275 billion each year they were in effect, based on an examination of previous EPA assessments and other research.The agency’s analysis also found that even a partial dismantling of the rules could lead to increased exposure to pollutants including smog, mercury, lead and fine particles, alongside higher greenhouse gas emissions.A wider reversal of US climate policyTrump has repeatedly rejected policies aimed at reducing human-caused climate change. He has called climate change “the greatest con job ever perpetrated on the world” and has described human-induced climate change as “a hoax”.His administration has also withdrawn the US from the 2015 Paris climate accord for a second time and moved to eliminate greenhouse gas standards for vehicle tailpipe emissions.The latest power-plant rollback represents a further reversal of policies pursued by both the Biden and Obama administrations to reduce industrial pollution and greenhouse gas emissions.Legal challenges are expected to follow because of the competing arguments underpinning the new rules.Meredith Hankins, a legal expert at the Natural Resources Defense Council, told news agency AFP that the administration’s two proposed moves appeared to have conflicting legal justifications.The technical repeal acknowledges, at least in its draft form, that the EPA has the authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions but argues that the Biden administration implemented the rules incorrectly.The broader proposal, meanwhile, is expected to argue that the agency lacks such authority altogether.“We’ll have to look at the final text of the rule,” Hankins said. “But I think on its face you can see the contradictions. So I’m certainly looking forward to seeing them in court.”The final rule is expected to provide a clearer picture of how far the Trump administration intends to go in restricting the EPA’s ability to regulate carbon emissions from the US power sector.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 3 Italian passengers fly out of Delhi without immigration clearance: What exactly happened
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The civil aviation ministry has issued a show-cause notice to Air India over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passenger.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The civil aviation ministry has issued a show-cause notice to Air India over alleged procedural lapses that allowed three Italian passengers to board a connecting flight from Delhi without completing immigration formalities earlier this month.The notice has been issued to the Air India CEO.The home ministry has also convened a meeting of stakeholders on Tuesday to discuss the incident, sources told news agency PTI.The three passengers flew from Amritsar to Delhi on September 4 before boarding a Lufthansa flight to Munich from Delhi airport. However, they did not complete the required immigration formalities at the airport, sources added.Titled “violation of SOP for hub and spoke operations resulting in three foreign nationals departing India without mandatory immigration clearance,” the show-cause notice issued to Air India last Saturday said the three passengers arrived in Delhi from Amritsar on AI 1115 at 12.50 am on September 4 and subsequently departed for Munich on a codeshare Lufthansa flight at 1.45 am, within an hour of their arrival.Home secretary Govind Mohan will chair a meeting on Tuesday to discuss the incident.The secretary and additional secretary of the civil aviation ministry, Intelligence Bureau director, additional secretary (UT and Foreigners) of the home ministry, Bureau of Immigration commissioner, Air India CEO and Delhi airport CEO are expected to attend the meeting, they added.What exactly happened?Amritsar airport is among the airports where Air India operates flights under its ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model. Under this arrangement, passengers complete immigration formalities at the airport of origin and can then travel to an overseas destination through a designated hub. At the hub airport, where the international flight departs, passengers are required only to undergo security checks before boarding.For a passenger travelling from Amritsar via Delhi to an international destination, Amritsar serves as the spoke and Delhi as the hub.In the case of the three Italian passengers, sources said they were issued boarding passes at Amritsar for both their flight to Delhi and the Lufthansa flight to Munich.However, as the two flights were not covered under Air India’s ‘Hub-and-Spoke’ model, the passengers were required to exit through the arrival area at Delhi and complete immigration formalities before taking the Lufthansa flight.After arriving at Delhi airport, they were instead taken to the international transfer area and did not reach the immigration counter. They then boarded the flight to Munich without completing the immigration process, the sources said, as cited by PTI.Air India and Lufthansa have an interline partnership. An interline agreement generally allows passengers to book connecting flights operated by different airlines under a single itinerary.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Police confirm 'targeted attack' after man named in suspected shooting
articles.summary: William Watson, known as Billy, was killed in the incident in West Lothian on Saturday.
articles.body:
A man killed in a suspected shooting at a house in West Lothian has been named locally as 35-year-old William Watson.

Police Scotland confirmed that the incident on Saturday in Harestanes Road, Armadale, was a targeted attack. It is investigating if a firearm was used.

Watson, known as Billy, died at the scene. The area remained cordoned off on Monday with officers posted outside the property.

Police are also investigating whether a nearby car fire in Netherhouses and a fire at a derelict house on Wotherspoon Road on Saturday are linked to the incident.

Uniformed officers were seen in the Netherhouses area where the car was set ablaze. A cordon was also put in place on Wotherspoon Road.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service said nobody was injured in the fires.

Police Scotland said Watson's death was being treated as suspicious and a postmortem examination would take place.

Supt Jocelyn Thomson said: "I understand people will be concerned about these incidents and a significant police presence remains in the area.

"However, this has been a targeted attack, and a team of experienced officers is working on the case.

"I have every confidence that they will find out who has committed this crime. Additional patrols will be in the area."

Kirsteen Sullivan, MP for Bathgate and Linlithgow, said the attack was "horrific and alarming".

"I want to extend my thoughts to local people who have been affected," she said.

"Police Scotland have advised that there is no immediate danger to the wider community and that this appears to have been an isolated incident.

"I would urge people to follow the advice of the police and not to speculate, particularly on social media, while the investigation is ongoing."

articles.title: Brazil election heats up: Lula, Flavio Bolsonaro locked in razor-thin runoff race
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Brazilian president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro are statistically tied in potential second-round matchups ahead .
articles.body: Brazilian president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and right-wing Senator Flavio Bolsonaro are statistically tied in potential second-round matchups ahead of Brazil’s October presidential election. Two opinion polls released on Monday showed the race tightening.According to the Reuters, aa BTG Pactual/Nexus survey put Lula narrowly ahead of Bolsonaro, 47 per cent to 46 per cent, in a simulated runoff. A separate Quaest poll commissioned by Globo showed Bolsonaro numerically ahead for the first time, leading Lula 42 per cent to 40 per cent.The latest figures mark a shift from the previous surveys. In the BTG Pactual/Nexus poll a week earlier, Bolsonaro led Lula 46 per cent to 45 per cent, his strongest showing in that survey since March. The September 7 Quaest poll had the two candidates tied at 41 per cent each.The BTG Pactual/Nexus survey also showed Lula maintaining a lead in the first round. He polled at 42 per cent, followed by Bolsonaro at 37 per cent, Augusto Cury at 6 per cent, Ronaldo Caiado at 5 per cent and Renan Santos at 2 per cent, according to the news agency.The poll surveyed 2,003 people between September 11 and 13, with a margin of error of two percentage points.In the Quaest first-round scenario, Lula led with 36 per cent, followed by Bolsonaro at 31 per cent. Quaest surveyed 2,004 people from September 10 to 13, also with a two-percentage-point margin of error.Flavio Bolsonaro, the eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, has emerged as Lula’s main challenger after receiving his father’s political backing. His stronger performance has also been welcomed by financial markets, with Brazilian assets rallying last week as investors viewed the senator as more market-friendly.The first round is scheduled for October 4. If no candidate secures more than 50 per cent of valid votes, the top two will face each other in a runoff on October 25.If Lula wins, he would surpass his own record as Brazil’s oldest elected president. The 80-year-old president is seeking another term as the closely fought race enters its final weeks.Bolsonaro has also sought to reassure voters about his approach to the election process. In an interview with TV Globo’s Jornal Nacional on Friday, he said, “I will respect the electoral process; I will respect the results.”His candidacy comes as his father serves a 27-year prison sentence after being convicted by Brazil’s Supreme Court over a plot to overturn his 2022 election defeat to Lula.Brazilian president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva told US President Donald Trump to “stay out” of Brazil’s October elections, while acknowledging his right to have an electoral preference. The remarks came during the July G7 summit in Switzerland, after Trump called Brazil “a little rough” and “dangerous politically”.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.summary: US News: Consul General of India in Los Angeles K J Srinivasa met and interacted with members of the SwimLife Orcas, a Masters swimming team from Bengaluru, fo.
articles.body: Consul General of India in Los Angeles K J Srinivasa met and interacted with members of the SwimLife Orcas, a Masters swimming team from Bengaluru, following their achievement in completing a double crossing of the Catalina Channel off the coast of Southern California.The six-member team completed the demanding two-way Catalina Channel relay on September 10–11, 2026, in 29 hours and 24 minutes, subject to final ratification. According to the team’s expedition report, the feat represents only the 12th successful double crossing of the Catalina Channel since 1991 and the first by an Asian team.Srinivasa congratulated the swimmers and their coach on the “extraordinary achievement”. He appreciated their physical endurance, mental resilience, discipline and exceptional teamwork, noting that their accomplishment was a matter of pride for India and the Indian community in the United States. He particularly commended the team for raising the Indian Tricolour on the shores of Southern California after completing an endurance challenge in one of the world’s demanding open-water environments.The SwimLife Orcas were guided by Coach Satish Kumar Mohan, 49, Founder of SwimLife Academy, Vice President of the Swimming Federation of India and Secretary of the Karnataka Swimming Association. The six swimmers comprised Meghana Mayya, 48, Senior Director–Technology at Lowe’s India; Varuna Mayya, 43, Principal Technical Specialist at Nokia Networks; Sindhu Naropanth, 41, Senior Tech Program Manager at Walmart Global Technologies; Nikhil Mysore Manjunath, 35, Associate Director at LTIMindtree; Siddhartha Agarwal, 52, Founder of Bhoruka Park; and team captain Sumanth Naropanth, 45, founder of Indian cybersecurity companies Deep Armor and Gauntlet.The team brings together accomplished professionals from India’s technology and business sectors with extensive experience in Masters and open-water swimming, according to the Indian consulate.“Several members have competed at State, National and International Masters championships and have previously participated in successful relay crossings of the English Channel, Catalina Channel and Palk Strait. Siddhartha Agarwal has also undertaken multiple relay and solo crossings and holds a Limca record for being the oldest Indian swimmer to successfully cross the English Channel,” said an official.The Catalina expedition tested the swimmers under formidable conditions. The channel stretches approximately 32 kilometres between Santa Catalina Island and the Southern California mainland, with currents, winds and ocean swells substantially increasing the effective swimming distance. The relay was conducted in one-hour rotations under Catalina Channel Swimming Federation regulations and was monitored by official observers.According to the consulate, Srinivasa observed that the achievement exemplified the determination, excellence and spirit of contemporary India, while also showcasing the ability of Indians from demanding professional careers to excel at the highest levels of endurance sport. articles.title: Pakistan weighs austerity measures as US-Iran war drives up fuel prices
articles.summary: Pakistan News: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices, as news agency PTI.
articles.body: Pakistan may bring back austerity measures to reduce fuel consumption as renewed fighting in West Asia drives up global oil prices, as news agency PTI cited Pak information minister Ataullah Tarar Monday.Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif has directed officials to examine which of the measures introduced earlier this year can be brought back, Tarar said at a press briefing attended by information technology minister Shaza Fatima Khawaja and petroleum minister Ali Pervaiz Malik."Austerity measures previously taken... are being reviewed to assess which of the previous measures need to be revived in the present situation," Tarar said.Pakistan had introduced the measures on March 9 as oil prices surged during the US-Iran war.The steps included halving fuel allowances for official vehicles, reducing lawmakers' salaries and allowing public sector employees to work from home for part of the week.The measures were withdrawn in June after the US and Iran entered a peace process. But renewed hostilities have once again pushed up international oil prices, putting pressure on fuel-importing countries such as Pakistan.Some restrictions, including shorter market hours, are already continuing, Tarar said.The government is facing the renewed pressure as petrol prices have climbed to PKR 375.82 per litre and high-speed diesel to PKR 403.32 per litre.To cushion the impact on smaller vehicle users, the government has announced a relief of Rs 100 per litre for motorcycles, rickshaws, Qingqi three-wheelers and vehicles with engine capacities of up to 800cc.Tarar said Sharif had asked deputy PM and foreign minister Ishaq Dar to make sure transport fares did not rise after the relief scheme was introduced.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
