articles.title: 'Triumph of truth over jhooth ki goonj': PM Modi hails BJP victory in Rajasthan civic polls
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday thanked the people of Rajasthan after the BJP emerged as the largest party in the state’s municipal .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Monday thanked the people of Rajasthan after the BJP emerged as the largest party in the state’s municipal elections, winning more wards than the Congress and securing majorities in four of the 10 municipal corporations.In a post on X, PM Modi said the results reflected support for the BJP’s policies of development and good governance under the “double-engine government”.“Heartfelt thanks to the people of Rajasthan for delivering a resounding victory to the BJP in the municipal elections,” PM Modi wrote.“This is a testament to the triumph of truth over the jhooth ki goonj (echo of lies),” he added.PM Modi also congratulated the winning candidates and BJP workers, saying the mandate would strengthen the party’s resolve to work towards development and prosperity in the state.BJP ahead of Congress in urban pollsAccording to figures from the Rajasthan State Election Commission, results for 10,235 of the state’s 10,244 wards had been declared by 8.30 pm on Monday.The BJP had won 4,179 wards compared with 3,613 for the Congress. The BJP crossed the majority mark in Jaipur, Udaipur, Kota and Bhilwara municipal corporations, while the Congress secured a majority in Bikaner.The Congress also recorded a major victory in the Jhalawar municipal council, considered a stronghold of former chief minister Vasundhara Raje.The elections covered 309 urban local bodies — 10 municipal corporations, 47 municipal councils and 252 municipal boards.BJP crosses majority in KotaIn Kota Municipal Corporation, the BJP secured 55 of the 100 wards, while Congress won 40 and Independents three. The result for Ward 87 was put on hold after an EVM malfunction.Congress candidate Laxmi Sharma and other party workers staged a protest outside the counting centre, seeking the result and alleging irregularities.Officials later sealed the machine in the presence of the district collector and additional district magistrate and forwarded a report to the Election Commission through the returning officer.The BJP also retained several individual seats. Vivek Rajvanshi won his fourth consecutive term from Ward 54, defeating Congress candidate Manish by 2,226 votes.Gopal Ram Manda secured his fifth consecutive election victory, defeating Congress candidate Sanjay Yadav by 899 votes.Congress and Independent candidates, however, registered victories in some key wards. Youth Congress candidate Arpit Jain defeated BJP veteran and former deputy mayor Yogendra Khinchi by 250 votes in Ward 86.Independent candidate Vandana Faujdar won Ward 71 with 1,264 votes, defeating BJP candidate Meenakshi Sen by 160 votes.Independents give BJP majority in BundiIn Bundi, the BJP initially emerged as the largest party with 29 wards, two short of a majority. Congress won 20 wards, while Independents secured 11.Later in the day, three Independent candidates, Prabhat Devi, Aatmaram Chopdar and Vishal Sharma, joined the BJP, taking the party to a majority and enabling it to form the board.The BJP had also captured the previous mid-term board after Congress council chairperson Madu Nuwal was suspended.Congress leaders had expected to retain control but faced criticism over ticket distribution. Former councillors Devraj Gochar, Ankit Buliwal and Jeeshan Ali, who were denied Congress tickets, won as Independents.BJP calls results a mandate for governanceBJP president Nitin Nabin thanked Rajasthan voters for what he described as a “historic victory”, saying the results showed continued faith in Modi’s leadership.BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi also cited the party’s performance in Kota, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had conducted the student-centric programme ‘Chhatron Ki Goonj’.“In Kota, where Rahul Gandhi had gone and attempted to create ‘jhooth ki goonj’, the BJP appears to be winning spectacularly,” Trivedi said.He claimed the results demonstrated that the Congress had “more propaganda and less reality” in its claims.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A Connecticut brass mill closed in 1986 and left behind a contaminated 66-acre site; 40 years later the town plans to turn it into a public works campus while converting its old yard into a riverside park
articles.summary: US News: Nearly 40 years after a brass mill shut down on the banks of the West Aspetuck River, the long-vacant industrial property in New Milford is finally be.
articles.body: Nearly 40 years after a brass mill shut down on the banks of the West Aspetuck River, the long-vacant industrial property in New Milford is finally being lined up for a new purpose, one that could turn a contaminated brownfield into a working municipal campus and, eventually, help create new public riverfront space elsewhere in town. The first step is surprisingly small: a three-story fire-training tower assembled from five repurposed shipping containers. The tower is proposed for the former Century Brass Mill property on Scovill Street, where the town plans to eventually build a 60,000-square-foot public works complex. The latest plans were reported by the News-Times and CT Insider, while New Milford’s 2026-27 budget confirms that the Century Brass project remains an active municipal priority.From factory floor to brownfieldCentury Brass was once a significant industrial presence in New Milford. The mill closed in 1986, leaving behind a large industrial property that would spend decades caught between environmental cleanup, demolition and redevelopment efforts.The site was contaminated with substances including PCBs and asbestos. After the town acquired the property through foreclosure in 1999, plans to clear the former mill became entangled in a legal dispute with a demolition contractor.That dispute ultimately went to court. In 2019, a Connecticut judge ruled in New Milford’s favor and awarded the town nearly $490,000 after finding that the contractor had breached its demolition contract. The state’s Appellate Court later upheld the town’s victory and sent the question of additional damages back for further consideration. The industrial buildings are now gone. What remains is a mostly vacant 66-acre property, with only a portion considered suitable for development.A new home for public worksThe town’s long-term plan is to move its public works operations from Young’s Field Road to the former brass mill property. The proposed campus would bring the engineering, highway and facilities departments together, while also providing space for fleet maintenance, indoor storage for vehicles and equipment and a helipad with a garage.Because wetlands and other environmental constraints limit the developable portion of the property, the town expects much of the site to remain natural. The fire-training tower would be the opening move. Firefighters would use the structure for smoke-filled training exercises, giving the town a practical facility while work toward the larger campus continues. The proposal still requires consideration by New Milford’s Zoning Commission.The cleanup is not quite the end of the storyThe redevelopment also shows how complicated the afterlife of an industrial property can be. New Milford has continued allocating money to the Century Brass project. The town’s 2026-27 budget includes funding for environmental work at the site, underscoring that redevelopment is taking place alongside the continuing obligations associated with the property’s industrial past.For a community that once watched the brass mill dominate this stretch of town, the eventual transformation could be significant: an abandoned factory site becoming a place where municipal crews maintain roads, equipment and public infrastructure. But the plan reaches beyond the former mill property.A riverside park could followMoving public works away from Young’s Field Road would free up the town’s existing materials-storage yard along the Housatonic River. The town envisions restoring that property and turning it into a small public park, with native vegetation and opportunities for passive recreation.That means the Century Brass redevelopment could ultimately produce two very different outcomes: an old industrial brownfield put back into productive use, and an existing municipal yard converted into green space beside the river. For New Milford, the transformation is less about erasing the past than finding a new use for land that has been waiting for one for decades.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: ‘Same government had closed the case’: Supriya Sule questions fresh CBI probe into Disha Salian’s death
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule on Monday questioned the registration of a CBI FIR into the death of Disha Salian, saying she was surprised be.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule on Monday questioned the registration of a CBI FIR into the death of Disha Salian, saying she was surprised because the case had earlier been treated as closed by the same government.Salian, a former manager of late actor Sushant Singh Rajput, died after falling from the 12th floor of a building in Mumbai’s Malad area on June 8, 2020. The CBI registered an FIR on September 13 following a direction from the Bombay High Court for a fresh probe into the circumstances surrounding her death.“I was surprised to hear how this (registration of an FIR by CBI) happened because it is the same government that had closed the case. I do not understand what is happening,” Sule told reporters in Pune.She said she would speak to Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Sanjay Raut to understand the latest developments.What is in the CBI FIR?According to CBI officials cited by news agency PTI, the FIR does not name any individual as an accused, in line with the Bombay High Court’s directions. It invokes IPC provisions relating to criminal conspiracy, gang rape, murder, disappearance of evidence and public servants allegedly framing incorrect records.The FIR followed a September 2 order by the Bombay High Court on a petition filed by Salian’s father, Satish Salian. The CBI began recording statements after the court directed it to conduct a thorough investigation.The court had criticised the Mumbai Police investigation, noting “glaring discrepancies” and observing that the probe “raises more questions than answers”.It had also directed that nobody should be treated as an accused unless investigators found sufficient grounds for reasonable suspicion based on the material collected during the probe.Advocate claims names are in FIRAdvocate Nilesh Ojha, who represents Satish Salian, claimed on Monday that the FIR contains the names of several individuals, including Shiv Sena (UBT) leader Aaditya Thackeray, Rohan Roy, Rhea Chakraborty, Param Bir Singh, Dino Morea and Sooraj Pancholi, among others.However, the CBI has not publicly confirmed the names claimed by the advocate, according to PTI.Ojha said the FIR was registered after the CBI conducted preliminary verification of Satish Salian’s complaint and recorded his statement. He said the case covers allegations of gang rape, murder and an alleged cover-up, invoking IPC Sections 376D, 302, 201, 217, 218 and 120B.Satish Salian had earlier approached the court alleging that his daughter was murdered.Speaking to news agency ANI on Friday, he said he had provided investigators with the names of people whom he wanted examined.“I stated the facts exactly as they were; I told them everything that happened to my daughter. I listed all the names: Aditya, Sooraj Pancholi, Dino Morea, and the bodyguards. They noted everything down,” he said.Sule raises political conspiracy claimAsked whether she saw a possible political conspiracy behind the development, Sule did not give a direct answer.“Anything is possible,” she said, while referring to what she called “ICE” — Income Tax, CBI and Enforcement Directorate — and alleging that central agencies had previously been used against political figures who later joined the ruling party.AIMIM leader Waris Pathan, meanwhile, said the case should not be politicised and should be left to the courts.“There is no need to give the Disha Salian case a political colour. There is no need to politicise it,” Pathan said, adding that the matter was sub judice and that “it is best to let the court decide”.Salian’s death had earlier been recorded as an Accidental Death Report. The Bombay High Court had raised concerns over the fact that no FIR was registered despite allegations by her family that she had been murdered.The court also noted that copies of the post-mortem report and ADR had not been provided to her family for years.Sushant Singh Rajput was found dead at his Bandra residence six days after Salian’s death.The CBI later submitted a closure report in Rajput’s case, concluding that he died by suicide; that report remains pending before the competent court.The Bombay High Court has directed the CBI to investigate the Salian case and has left it to the agency to determine whether a criminal case is made out based on the evidence collected.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.body: Saturday night, Colin Kaepernick and Jemele Hill spoke at the National Black Footwear Forum in Detroit, Michigan. I started seeing a very cute Black girl named Crystal. Right away, I noticed how different I felt with her than in my own home. I could talk to Crystal, really talk to her, without having to explain myself; it was a remarkable discovery, being understood up front and without question. When I visited her home, I was stunned by how warm and welcoming her family was. I immediately felt comfortable there," he begins. "I asked Crystal to the homecoming dance, a formal affair involving fancy gowns, tuxedoes, and corsages. We had a nice time at the dance. When I got the official portrait from that night, featuring me and Crystal posed up in that classic, airbrushed frame, my mother hid it away in the back of a drawer." "My mother convinced me to ask Lindsay, the daughter of one of her friends, to the next formal dance. Lindsay was white. When I brought that picture home, my mother promptly plastered it on the wall for all to see. In her mind, Crystal was just a phase. Lindsay was the kind of girl I should want. Years later, when I was in the NFL, she told me that I should ask out Taylor Swift (long before Travis Kelce made his move) because we would be perfect together. articles.title: Norway’s Green Mountain data centre uses 8°C fjord water to cool its servers, turning a naturally cold resource into free refrigeration
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A data centre quietly produces heat every second it is operating. Behind the walls, rows of servers process data continuously, turning large amounts o.
articles.body: A data centre quietly produces heat every second it is operating. Behind the walls, rows of servers process data continuously, turning large amounts of electricity into computing power and, inevitably, excess heat. That heat has to be removed to keep the equipment within safe operating temperatures, adding significantly to the facility’s energy demand. Green Mountain has approached the problem differently at its Norwegian sites, using the country's naturally cool conditions as part of the cooling infrastructure. At one facility, water drawn from a nearby fjord remains at about 8°C at depth. Instead of making cold mechanically, engineers use this naturally chilled water to carry heat away.How data centre cooling keeps servers running safelyServers turn electricity into computing power, but a large share of that energy eventually becomes heat. Keeping temperatures within operating limits therefore becomes a permanent requirement, with cooling systems running alongside the IT equipment.Green Mountain says conventional data centre cooling can require an additional 40 to 80% of the electricity used to power the servers. That makes the cooling system an important part of a facility's total energy performance, particularly at sites operating continuously.The company uses what is commonly called free cooling, or natural cooling. The basic idea is straightforward: instead of producing cold through energy-intensive mechanical refrigeration, the facility makes use of naturally cold air or water already available outside.How 8°C fjord water cools the data centreAt Green Mountain's SVG-Rennesøy site, the cooling source is the fjord immediately beside the data centre. The location has a particular underwater structure. The entrance to the fjord is relatively shallow, while the central section reaches considerable depth.Reportedly, at depths below roughly 75 metres, the water stays at about 8°C. Green Mountain installed intake pipes reaching down to around 100 metres, allowing the facility to access that cold water throughout the year.The water does not simply flow through the server rooms. Instead, it enters a cold-water basin and passes through a titanium heat exchanger. Heat from the data centre's separate chilled-water circuit is transferred to the cold seawater, which is then returned to the fjord.That arrangement keeps the two water systems separate.How the cooling system uses gravity and recycled waterThere is an unusual simplicity to the way the cold fjord water reaches the facility. The intake is designed so that water can enter the cold-water basin through gravity rather than being pumped up from the seabed. Inside the facility, a closed-loop freshwater system circulates through the cooling infrastructure. The same chilled water can continue moving around the data centre without being consumed as part of the cooling process.Once it has absorbed heat through the heat exchanger, the seawater is discharged back into the fjord. Green Mountain says the warmed discharge does not create a negative environmental impact.The company also lists an energy figure for the system of 3 kW of power for 1,000 kW of cooling, illustrating how little electrical energy is needed for the cooling process itself compared with conventional refrigeration.What PUE reveals about data centre energy useData centre operators commonly use Power Usage Effectiveness, or PUE, to assess how much energy a facility consumes beyond the electricity delivered directly to its IT equipment. A PUE of 1.0 would mean all the facility's electricity went to computing equipment. Real data centres are higher because they also need power for cooling, lighting, electrical infrastructure, security systems and other supporting equipment.Green Mountain designed its facilities to reach a PUE of 1.2 or lower and says it frequently records values close to 1.10. The company attributes much of this performance to its cooling approach. For comparison, it cites an Uptime Institute average PUE of 1.56 for 2019.Even the electrical infrastructure itself contributes to the figure. UPS systems, which protect servers against power interruptions, lose some energy when converting electricity between forms. Green Mountain estimates that a typical redundant UPS arrangement can add a partial PUE of about 1.06 to 1.10 before transformer losses and other requirements are considered.How Green Mountain keeps its cooling system protectedThe fjord water never becomes the air circulating through the server rooms. Heat is transferred through the titanium exchanger, while the chilled freshwater remains in its own circuit. That separation is useful for more than water management. The environment inside the data centre does not have to be exposed directly to outside humidity, pollutants or other contaminants carried in by air.The cooling infrastructure is also duplicated. Green Mountain uses an N+N arrangement, meaning the cooling station, pipework and pumps have redundant counterparts. Both systems can operate during normal conditions, while the design allows maintenance to take place without taking the entire cooling arrangement offline.Under the server-room floor, chilled water is supplied through duplicated routes. The facility can also accommodate different cooling requirements, from conventional server densities to higher-density installations reaching up to 40 kW per square metre.How Green Mountain keeps its cooling system efficientThe fjord system relies on relatively few moving components, with circulation pumps doing much of the mechanical work. That reduces the number of parts that require regular servicing compared with a more complicated refrigeration installation.Green Mountain also says the intake location has little algae growth, which helps reduce cleaning requirements for the titanium heat exchanger.The cooling station is connected to the site's data centre infrastructure management system. Its operation is automated, with the system adjusting to changes in demand and continuously reporting its condition.There is also an environmental benefit in avoiding some synthetic refrigerants. Conventional refrigeration systems can rely on gases such as hydrofluorocarbons, which can present an environmental risk if they escape into the atmosphere.How 330 days of free cooling works at RjukanNot every data centre has a deep, cold body of water sitting next to it. Green Mountain uses a different form of free cooling at its TEL-Rjukan facility, where the surrounding Norwegian climate provides the cold source.There, an indirect air-cooling system uses outside air to remove heat through a heat exchanger. The air entering the server environment remains in a separate closed circuit, rather than being brought directly into the data rooms.At Rjukan, Green Mountain says the system can provide free cooling for around 330 days a year. The site's median temperature is about 13°C, and its location receives little direct sunlight during part of the year, conditions that help reduce the need for mechanical cooling.During warmer summer periods, water can be introduced on the outside-air side of the cooling equipment. Evaporating that water lowers the temperature available to the cooling system and extends the period in which it can operate efficiently.How the Rjukan cooling system scales with server demandThe Rjukan system was developed with scalability in mind. Its cooling equipment is built in individual units rated at either 250 kW or 500 kW.That means capacity does not have to be installed all at once. As more computing equipment is added, further cooling units can be incorporated into the infrastructure.The approach is also designed around hot-aisle containment, directing heat away from server equipment and allowing the cooling system to deal with it more efficiently. With limited piping and relatively few moving parts, Green Mountain says the design reduces both maintenance requirements and the number of components that could fail.The two Norwegian sites use different natural resources, but the principle is much the same. At Rennesøy, the cooling system takes advantage of water that is already cold. At Rjukan, it makes use of the temperature of the outside air.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.body: A Cleveland district that once had nearly 100,000 residents in the 1960s now has fewer than 20,000, leaving large areas with open green space that can resemble the countryside. The city is now trying to reverse that decline through a new Housing Innovation District and plans to support the construction of 200 new homes.The effort received a boost after Ohio announced $14 million in grants for workforce housing across 10 counties, local media NEOtrans reported. Cleveland is set to receive $2 million, which will support the creation of the 200 housing units on the city’s near-East Side.The Housing Innovation District covers significant parts of the Central, Hough and St Clair-Superior neighbourhoods. The area has seen major population loss over the decades, leaving vacant land and large stretches of greenery between existing buildings.The new housing investment is linked to wider plans to bring jobs, infrastructure and development to the near-East Side. Cleveland City Council authorised the Housing Innovation District in August and approved a tax increment financing, or TIF, mechanism to support public improvements in the area.From a crowded area to an urban prairieThe scale of the population change is visible across parts of Cleveland’s East Side. The area had nearly 100,000 residents in the 1960s but now has fewer than 20,000.That decline has changed the physical appearance of some neighbourhoods. Areas that were once more densely occupied now include vacant plots and large stretches of open land. Parts of the East Side look rural, with the loss of population creating what it called an “urban prairie”.The Housing Innovation District is intended to respond to housing demand created by investments involving Amazon Services, LLC and the City of Cleveland.Nearby, the Cleveland Midline Priority Investment Area involves 350 acres of land being assembled, cleaned and marketed for commercial redevelopment.TIF could generate up to $182 millionThe $2 million state grant is only one part of the planned investment. Cleveland’s TIF mechanism is expected to generate between $64 million and $182 million over 30 years. That money is intended to support public improvements, including streets, sewers and parks.Mayor Justin Bibb welcomed the state funding and said it would add to other efforts already under way in the city, including the Midline Priority Investment Area.“This funding is a sign that our Housing Innovation District is much more than just an idea. It’s a real, tangible solution towards homeownership, entrepreneurship, modern housing, and neighborhood stability,” Bibb said. He also thanked Governor Mike DeWine and his administration for investing in the work.Ohio expands workforce housing supportThe Cleveland award came from the second round of Ohio’s Residential Economic Development District, or REDD, programme. The programme is providing up to $15 million in grants during the fiscal year to help communities expand housing opportunities near major economic development projects.The Ohio Department of Development received 32 eligible applications during this funding round. Together, those applications requested nearly $69 million.Cleveland was among the communities receiving one of the larger awards. Cincinnati, Piketon and Toledo also received $2 million each. Bowling Green, Columbus, Heath, Niles, Oberlin and Xenia received $1 million each.Ohio Governor Mike DeWine said housing needs to be available near new employment opportunities. “As we continue bringing new jobs and new opportunities to our great state, we need to make sure the people filling those jobs can find a home nearby,” DeWine said in a written statement.He added that the awards would help communities support new growth and give more Ohio residents opportunities to live and work in those areas.Lt Governor Jim Tressel said new businesses can create opportunities, but communities also need infrastructure to benefit from that growth. “We all know that new businesses can bring tremendous opportunities, but our communities ultimately need the right foundation to make the most of it,” Tressel said.He said the investments would help local partners prepare for future growth by supporting housing and infrastructure needed by the workforce.Housing linked to jobs and infrastructureThe REDD programme was signed into law by DeWine last year. Local governments within 20 miles of a major economic development project could apply for funding.The grants can be used for housing-related infrastructure, public safety and community services, or capital support for new housing development.Ohio Department of Development Director Lydia Mihalik said communities of different sizes have a role in the state’s growth.“Every community has an important role to play in Ohio’s continued growth.
